1. \*\*5′ cap اضافه می‌شود\*\*
به ابتدای RNA یک مولکول تغییر‌یافته به نام \*\*7-methylguanosine\*\* وصل می‌شود.

\`exon 1 — intron — exon 2 — intron — exon 3\`

بعد:
\`exon 1 — exon 2 — exon 3\`

برای همین lecture گفته \*\*scissors + tape\*\*:
\*\*scissors = بریدن intronها\*\*
\*\*tape = چسباندن exonها به هم\*\*. \[PubMed\](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21084389/?utm\_source=chatgpt.com)

TOPIC: Pre-mRNA processing

KEY IDEA
Many eukaryotic protein-coding transcripts undergo 5′ capping, 3′-end formation and splicing.

EXPLANATION
These processing steps help create export- and translation-competent mRNA.

WHY IT MATTERS
Use this concept to interpret the related biological data or computational method with its assumptions visible.

IMPORTANT LIMITATION
The order and coupling of processing steps are more complex than a strict linear cartoon.

ACTIVE-RECALL QUESTION

Answer: 5′ capping, splicing, 3′-end cleavage/polyadenylation

EVIDENCE STATUS: BACKGROUND (Saved research note; reference supports topic, not necessarily every claim).
Supporting reading: Wilkinson, Charenton & Nagai, Annu Rev Biochem (2020) — https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-biochem-091719-064225

EXPANDED CONTEXT FROM ORIGINAL NOTE
Typical processing of a eukaryotic protein-coding primary transcript includes addition of a 5′ 7-methylguanosine cap, spliceosome-mediated removal of relevant introns, and cleavage plus polyadenylation at the 3′ end. The cap and poly(A) tail affect stability, export and translation, while alternative splicing can produce multiple isoforms. Processing is frequently co-transcriptional, so the steps are not required to occur in the neat sequence shown by a teaching diagram. Example precursor: exon 1–intron–exon 2–intron–exon 3; a spliced product joins the exons. A mature exported mRNA may then be translated by cytoplasmic ribosomes.
